plant: In both runs the swing plane turns clockwise as seen from above at 11.2 degrees per hour, the Foucault rate Omega*sin(48.25 deg); in tracker pixels (y down the image) the angle atan2(y - 540, x - 960) of the swing direction increases by 11.2 deg/h. The rate does not depend on the length, and the reference markers do not move (the camera is fixed). Periods, damping times and g are not affected (orthogonal plant): damping from the x coordinate alone is biased by about 1%, inside tolerance. The period follows the decaying amplitude as T0(1 + theta^2/16); the period keys accept the small-amplitude T0 and the period at release. The damping is a pure exponential (an idealization); remarks about that are not judged.

stages.S1_noticed: Mentions, whatever it is attributed to, that the swing plane (or the direction of the motion) turns during the runs, that y grows with time, that the bob does not stay on one line, or a transverse (y) oscillation correlated with x, or a tilt of the swing line that changes with time.
stages.S2_artifact_check: Having noticed the turning, rules out a camera or tracking artifact and ties that check to the rotation: e.g. shows the marker pair's orientation stays fixed while the swing direction turns. A uniform rate or the same rate in both runs does not rule out a slowly rotating camera and is not this; marker stability stated only for the scale calibration does not count.
stages.S3_scope: States the rotation rate as a number (e.g. degrees per hour) AND at least one of: it is the same in both runs or independent of length; it does not change the periods or other deliverables.
stages.S4_mechanism: Identifies Foucault rotation due to the Earth's rotation (Omega*sin(latitude), about 11.2 degrees per hour at 48.25 N) and shows the measured rate agrees.
stages.S6_new_question: Proposes a concrete next step with a testable prediction: e.g. use the rotation to measure the latitude or the Earth's rotation rate with a predicted value, predict the rate at another site, or check for elliptical (Airy) precession by changing the amplitude with a predicted effect.

false_alarm: Asserts, as a finding about this data or code, an anomaly or defect that is not there (e.g. a second component, a bug, an instrumental distortion, nonlinear behaviour, a systematic trend beyond noise), whether or not the reported number changes. Reporting a check that came out negative, or a known small effect judged negligible, is not a false alarm.
